case_name: Sanjay Chandra v. Central Bureau of Investigation

pages.text:
REPORTABLE
IN THE SUPREME COURT OF INDIA
CRIMINAL APPELLATE JURISDICTION
CRIMINAL APPEAL NO. 2178 OF 2011

SANJAY CHANDRA ... APPELLANT
VERSUS
CENTRAL BUREAU OF INVESTIGATION ... RESPONDENT

JUDGMENT

H.L. DATTU, J.

1. In the present appeal, the appellants are seeking bail in connection with alleged economic offenses involving cheating under Section 420 and criminal conspiracy under Section 120B of the Indian Penal Code, 1860.

2. The primary question is whether detention in judicial custody pending trial should be used as a punitive measure. The object of bail is neither punitive nor preventive. Deprivation of liberty must be considered a punishment, unless it can be required for ensuring that an accused person will stand his trial when called upon.

3. The grant of bail under Section 439 of the CrPC must balance the gravity of the economic offense with the constitutional guarantee under Article 21. Merely because the offense is of serious nature or involves high financial stakes, the accused cannot be incarcerated indefinitely when the investigation is complete and the charge-sheet has been filed.

4. As observed in State of Rajasthan v. Balchand (1977) 4 SCC 308, the basic rule may perhaps be tersely put as bail, not jail, except where there are circumstances suggestive of fleeing from justice or repeating offenses.
